claude.sample_unit: patients with MCI (363 in independent test set)

links.outcome: Intermediate-risk group size and PPV/NPV under 90% vs 95% sensitivity/specificity dual cutoffs
links.effect: 90% strategy limited intermediate-risk group to 27.3% (n=99) vs 49.6% (n=180) for 95%; accuracy 87.5% vs 89.1%; PPV 83.3% vs 86.2%; NPV 90.4% vs 90.7%.
links.quote: This strategy limited the intermediate-risk group to 27.3% of patients, enabling definitive risk classification for 72.7% of the cohort with 87.5% overall accuracy ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Generalizability across sites and acquisition devices
links.effect: Single-center cohort with a single PET/CT scanner model; no external validation and no validation on routine clinical CT.
links.quote: First, this study was conducted within a single-center cohort (K-ROAD), and the model has not been externally validated in geographically or ethnically diverse populations.

unlisted_practices: Dual-cutoff three-tier risk stratification to reduce definitive misclassification
Use of low-dose CT from PET attenuation correction as an MRI alternative for prognosis

links.effect: Independent test set (n=363): AUC 0.870, accuracy 0.793, sensitivity 0.701, specificity 0.861.
links.quote: On the independent test set (n=363), the logistic regression model achieved an AUC of 0.870, with accuracy of 0.793, sensitivity of 0.701, and specificity of 0.861 ( Supplementary Fig. 1B ).

links.effect: Among six classifiers, logistic regression had the highest cross-validation AUC, 0.861±0.012.
links.quote: Logistic regression achieved the highest cross-validation AUC (0.861±0.012) and was selected for subsequent analyses ( Supplementary Fig. 1A ).

links.effect: 90% strategy intermediate-risk 27.3% (n=99) vs 49.6% (n=180) for 95%; accuracy 87.5% vs 89.1%.
links.quote: The 90% strategy was superior for clinical triage, limiting the intermediate-risk group to 27.3% (n=99) compared to 49.6% (n=180) in the 95% strategy.

links.effect: For 90% risk categories, low-risk NPV was 90.4% and high-risk PPV was 83.3%.
links.quote: The low-risk group achieved 90.4% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84.6%–94.5%) NPV and the high-risk group achieved 83.3% (95% CI, 74.9%–89.8%) PPV.

links.outcome: intermediate-risk classification rate and triage accuracy
links.effect: 90% strategy limited intermediate-risk classifications to 27.3% (n=99) with 87.5% accuracy, versus 49.6% (n=180) with 89.1% accuracy for 95% strategy
links.quote: The 90% strategy was superior for clinical triage, limiting the intermediate-risk group to 27.3% (n=99) compared to 49.6% (n=180) in the 95% strategy.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a deep learning model for predicting dementia conversion from low-dose CT scans and explicitly tests/compares operational risk-stratification cutoff strategies (90% vs 95% sensitivity/specificity operating targets) to optimize clinical triage workflow.
